explanation: A null subtree has depth zero. For every node return one plus the larger child depth.
timeComplexity: O(n) time for n nodes. Each node combines two child depths once.
spaceComplexity: O(h) recursion space for tree height h. The active recursion chain has at most h frames.
attribution: Original repository-authored Blind75 Python algorithm, promoted from the validated correct fixtures. Collection membership follows Crackr; no external solution service is used.
correctness: The empty subtree has depth zero. Every root-to-leaf path through a nonempty node continues through exactly one child, so the longest has one node plus the greater child depth. Applying this recurrence bottom-up gives the maximum depth of the root.
walkthrough: For [4,2,8,null,3,null,9,null,5], the longest branch is 4→2→3→5. It has four nodes, so return depth 4; the other branch 4→8→9 is shorter.
edgeCases: The empty tree has depth zero.
A skew tree may require a recursion stack as tall as its node count.
